country.comment: Study conducted in the municipality (commune) of Kye-Ossi in South Cameroon (Sud-Cameroun).
country.where_found: PDF p. 1, Title & Affiliations; PDF p. 2, English Title & Abstract

effect_estimate.comment: Descriptive mixed-methods diagnostic with no inferential regression or causal effect size; note minor internal text discrepancy on household pit-latrine shares (Abstract states 47% use improved pit latrines, whereas Results/Figure 2 report 33% improved pit latrines, 25% rudimentary pit latrines, and 12% modern latrines, and Discussion states 83% use pit latrines overall).
effect_estimate.value: Descriptive mixed-methods diagnostic (no inferential statistical effect estimate reported): Kye-Ossi (~75,000 inhabitants) has neither a public piped water distribution network nor a municipal sanitation/latrine-emptying service; institutional analysis documents unclear, overlapping mandates and no coordination platform among 5 local state/municipal bodies (MINEE, MINEPDED, MINADER, MINSANTE, Mairie de Kye-Ossi), insufficient decentralized municipal funding, and contractor non-compliance with regulatory drilling standards. Empirically, 12 of 33 hand-pump boreholes (36%) are non-functional, 7 of 7 modern wells (4 community, 3 private) are functional, and 6 of 7 pay public toilets (4/4 private, 2/3 municipal) are functional. Among 200 surveyed urban households, drinking water comes from boreholes (40%), wells (17%), springs (6%), unknown vendor sources (4%), and bottled water (3%); 71% consume water untreated (29% treat water); only 26% are satisfied with drinking water supply (74% dissatisfied) while 69% are satisfied with basic sanitation; 12% use modern latrines (33% improved pit latrines and 25% rudimentary pit latrines in Fig. 2; 47% improved pit latrines in Abstract) and only 12.5% of public primary schools have modern latrines. Water is sold at 100 FCFA per 20 L container and public toilet fees are 50–100 FCFA per use.
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 1, Résumé; PDF p. 2, Abstract; PDF pp. 4–8, Résultats, Tableaux 1–4 & Figures 1–3; PDF pp. 9–10, Discussion & Conclusion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Capped at 2 by the mixed-methods design ceiling (MMAT). Primary semi-structured interviews with municipal sector officials and service providers, community focus groups, and physical GPS facility audits directly document institutional fragmentation, lack of municipal funding and coordination platforms under decentralization, user fee burdens, and non-compliance with regulatory borehole construction standards operating on local water and sanitation provision.
